newsitem.title: UK: LME copper stock falls mostly re-location - analyst.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stock falls mostly re-location - analyst.

text.p: The substantial drawdowns in London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouse stocks of copper seen in October do not reflect a fundamental market deficit, industry analysts Bloomsbury Minerals Economics (BME) said.

In a review of the market BME analyst Peter Hollands said that the global copper market supply/demand balance could not have turned from an annualised seasonally adjusted rate of surplus of 60,000 tonnes a year in third quarter 1996 to a deficit of one million tonnes by October.
"Certainly not when production is growing faster than consumption," he said.

"Close to 100 percent of the October LME stock drawdown reflected re-location (mainly from Western Europe to China, but also to the U.S., Korea and elsewhere), not some huge instantaneous global market deficit," BME said.

Looking at the overall global picture BME downgraded its projection of the 1996 copper market surplus to 50,000 tonnes from a previous 100,000 tonnes. This is because previous estimates of Russian copper production and cathode stocks in Rotterdam were too high.
Split into regional areas the Western market will be in deficit by 50,000 tonnes, while the Eastern bloc will show a surplus of 100,000 tonnes.
